newsitem.title: USA: National-Standard seeks to cut more costs.
newsitem.headline: National-Standard seeks to cut more costs.

text.p: National-Standard Co said on Thursday it would continue to focus on reducing costs and improving profit margins even though its net income for fiscal 1996 jumped by 20 percent.

"Continued pressure on pricing made it difficult to maintain our margins, although significant progress was made in certain areas," said Michael Savitske, National-Standard president and chief executive officer.
"We will continue to focus on cost reduction and margin improvement in conjunction with our actions related to growing the air-bag and weld-wire segments," he said in a statement.
For its fiscal year ended September 30, National-Standard reported net income rose to $8.9 million from $7.4 million in fiscal 1995. Fiscal 1996 sales totaled $248.6 million, a gain of 0.5 percent.
Shares of National-Standard, which makes wire and wire-related products, were unchanged at seven.
